Direct Known Subclasses:
HadurRecorder
public class Hadur extends robocode.TeamRobot
The Robocode adapter. It turns engine events and getters into a BotInput, hands it to the core through the Guard, and applies the BotOrders that come back. All strategy lives in hadur2.core; this class only translates.

The core is static so what it learns survives from round to round, as Robocode creates a new robot instance each round.

From A4 the adapter is a TeamRobot, so one class plays all three ladders and one memory serves them: it passes the roster into the battle's facts, hands teammates' messages to the core and broadcasts the core's. Off a team getTeammates() is null, no message arrives and none is sent, so it behaves as the AdvancedRobot it was.

One turn, as the engine runs it:

  1. During execute() the engine delivers the turn's events, in its own priority order, to the handlers below; each becomes a BotEvent in pending.
  2. The run loop puts the last core tick's duration first, as a BotEvent.TickTime (TIME-1), then builds a BotInput from the getters and the pending events.
  3. Guard.tick(hadur2.core.model.BotInput) runs the core. If the core throws, the guard returns the safe order set for this tick and records the fault (RES-1), so this loop always has orders to apply.
  4. apply turns the orders into setter calls, and execute() ends the turn.

Round and battle ends go to the core too: roundEnded once per round for the R record (RES-5), a profile checkpoint when the round ends with Hadur alive and a final save at the battle's end (MEM-3). The three protected hooks exist for HadurRecorder; the robot itself does nothing in them.

The adapter holds mutable statics (core, guard, console). CORE-2's ban on them covers hadur2.core only, and here they are the point: a static survives the new robot instance Robocode creates each round.

  • Field Details

    • TICK_ALLOWANCE_NANOS

      static final long TICK_ALLOWANCE_NANOS
      The per-turn time the tick budget assumes (TIME-1). A robot cannot read the engine's CPU constant, so this is a fixed guess: the bench machine's constant is about 3 ms. The core's tick budget drops a computation level after a tick that used more than 70% of it.
      See Also:

    • warmUp

      static Set<RoleId> warmUp(double width, double height, int others)
      TIME-5: runs one tick for each role of the charter through a throwaway core and guard before the real battle begins, so that class loading and JIT warm-up land here rather than on the first real tick a role drives. No store (nothing is read or written) and no telemetry from the throwaway core itself; the core, guard and result are all discarded, and nothing they do reaches the real core.

      Each tick carries a synthetic scan, not just a bare one: a tick with no scan takes only the "enemy not seen yet" branch, which never reaches the aiming, movement and memory-adjacent code the real first scan will actually run, so it would warm little of what needs it. In a melee the Melee drives the first tick with every opponent alive, and the Duel the second with one left, the hand-off included (A3). A failure here is logged, not silent: it never stops the battle (a cold real tick still runs correctly), but it is worth knowing about.

      Returns:
      the roles that drove a warm-up tick
